title: Reviewing the step-up every year
objectives: Decide when the step-up should slow rather than grow.
body_md:
Review the step-up at every annual SIP review, alongside the goal and the asset mix.

## The annual check

- Did income grow as expected? If not, keep the step-up smaller this year rather than cancelling the SIP.
- Is the instalment still comfortable? A SIP that feels heavy is at risk of being stopped.
- Is the goal on track or ahead? If ahead, the step-up can slow down.
- Has the cap been reached? Decide whether to raise it, keep it, or start a new SIP.
- Does the bank mandate still cover the next instalment?
- Is the step-up money going to the right asset mix? As a goal nears, new money may go to debt instead.

## The principle

The step-up is a dial, not a switch. Small adjustments each year keep the SIP alive; an all-or-nothing approach produces cancellations.
example: At the review, income grew 6% not 10%, so the step-up is held at 5% for the year, the cap is unchanged, and the new money is redirected to debt because the goal is now three years away.
say: Let's check the step-up against your income, your comfort and the goal.
If income didn't grow as expected, we'll hold the step-up rather than cancel the SIP.
never: The step-up runs on its own; no review needed.
If you can't afford it this year, cancel the SIP.

check.q: What should happen at the annual review if income grew less than expected?
o: Keep the step-up smaller this year rather than cancelling
check.why: Hold or lower the step-up; never cancel the SIP over one weak year.

check.q: The goal is now ahead of plan. What does that mean for the step-up?
o: It should move to a sectoral fund
check.why: If the goal is ahead, the step-up can slow; the plan is working.

check.q: Which item belongs in the annual step-up check?
o: Income, comfort, goal progress, cap, mandate and asset mix
check.why: All six, every year, at the same review as the goal and the mix.
